-- ── The raid-target mark atlas (ref TargetFrame.lua l.460-463 + l.475-484) ────────────── -- `Interface\TargetingFrame\UI-RaidTargetingIcons` is one 256x256 sheet of 4x4 64px cells, -- in mark order: star, circle, diamond, triangle, moon, square, cross, skull. The helper -- turns a 1..8 mark index into that cell's texcoords on a CALLER-SUPPLIED texture — it owns -- no frame and reads no unit, which is why an addon can hand it a texture of its own. -- -- Three corpus addons do, in two codebases (`Optional` and `oRA2` ship the same two files): -- CustomNameplates options.lua:363 (its options preview) -- Optional / oRA2 MainTank.lua:1216, PlayerTarget.lua:1472 -- We answer `GetRaidTargetIndex(unit)` already (0434 §6); this is the other half — what an -- addon DRAWS with that number — and without it those lines raise while redrawing a mark. -- -- KEPT WHOLE, INCLUDING THE REFERENCE'S OWN SLIP: the row is derived with -- `/ RAID_TARGET_TEXTURE_ROWS` while the column uses `mod(.., RAID_TARGET_TEXTURE_COLUMNS)`. -- Rows and columns are both 4, so the two agree for every index this sheet holds and the -- output is right; "fixing" it to divide by COLUMNS computes the same coords today and would -- quietly diverge from the client the day a caller changes a constant. These are globals in -- the reference for exactly that reason — addons read them, and two of ours are addons that -- draw their own marks. RAID_TARGET_ICON_DIMENSION = 64 RAID_TARGET_TEXTURE_DIMENSION = 256 RAID_TARGET_TEXTURE_COLUMNS = 4 RAID_TARGET_TEXTURE_ROWS = 4
function SetRaidTargetIconTexture(texture, raidTargetIconIndex) raidTargetIconIndex = raidTargetIconIndex - 1 local left, right, top, bottom local coordIncrement = RAID_TARGET_ICON_DIMENSION / RAID_TARGET_TEXTURE_DIMENSION left = mod(raidTargetIconIndex, RAID_TARGET_TEXTURE_COLUMNS) * coordIncrement right = left + coordIncrement top = floor(raidTargetIconIndex / RAID_TARGET_TEXTURE_ROWS) * coordIncrement bottom = top + coordIncrement texture:SetTexCoord(left, right, top, bottom) end

-- Wire an instance to its unit token (called from each frame's OnLoad), cache its child -- widgets, register the event set, and do the first paint. deadText is target-only -- (getglobal returns nil for the player, which has no DEAD region) — guarded at use. function BenillaUnitFrame_OnLoad(frame, unit) frame.unit = unit local name = frame:GetName() frame.healthbar = getglobal(name .. "HealthBar") frame.manabar = getglobal(name .. "ManaBar") -- TWO prefixes, both the reference's own. The bars are named off the FRAME -- (`PlayerFrameHealthBar`, ref-PlayerFrame.xml l.288) but the art, text and icons are -- named off the UNIT (`PlayerName` l.58, `PlayerPortrait` l.35, `TargetDeadText` -- ref-TargetFrame.xml l.173) — flat globals, which is what an addon reaches for. -- `short` is the frame name minus its trailing "Frame". local short = string.sub(name, 1, string.len(name) - 5) -- Our ring art rides a $parentTextureFrame child (the reference nests two ANONYMOUS -- frames there instead, ref-PlayerFrame.xml l.49-51), so the frame whose level the bars -- are pushed under is still named off the frame. local tf = name .. "TextureFrame" -- The recessed-bar look, the reference's own mechanism (ref-TargetFrame.lua l.32-34): -- push the bars one frame level BELOW the ring art's TextureFrame. Frame level is the -- only key term above the draw layer (decision 0884), so this is the only thing that can -- hold a BACKGROUND ring texture over an ARTWORK bar fill. See the LAYERING note up top. local textureFrameLevel = getglobal(tf):GetFrameLevel() frame.healthbar:SetFrameLevel(textureFrameLevel - 1) frame.manabar:SetFrameLevel(textureFrameLevel - 1) -- The on-bar numerals (TextStatusBar.xml, decision 1082; the switch that shows them -- is 1140's Status Bar Text). Wiring is unconditional — a frame with no text regions -- gets a no-op, since SetTextStatusBarText drops a nil text and UpdateTextString skips -- a bar with no TextString — so the target frame is one FontString pair away from -- having them the day its hover lands. `textLockable` is the REFERENCE's own split -- and the only conditional here: 1.12 sets it on the player's two bars, the pet's two -- and the XP bar, and on nothing else, which is exactly why Status Bar Text pins your -- own numbers and your pet's but never the target's (decision 1143). if TextStatusBar_Initialize then -- engine tests load file subsets TextStatusBar_Initialize(frame.healthbar) TextStatusBar_Initialize(frame.manabar) SetTextStatusBarText(frame.healthbar, getglobal(name .. "HealthBarText")) SetTextStatusBarText(frame.manabar, getglobal(name .. "ManaBarText")) if unit == "player" then frame.healthbar.textLockable = 1 frame.manabar.textLockable = 1 end end -- The hover seam (1146): who this bar belongs to, and what its click means. local click = TargetFrame_OnClick if unit == "player" then click = PlayerFrame_OnClick end frame.healthbar.owner = frame frame.manabar.owner = frame frame.healthbar.ownerClick = click frame.manabar.ownerClick = click frame.nameText = getglobal(short .. "Name") frame.levelText = getglobal(short .. "LevelText") frame.deadText = getglobal(short .. "DeadText") -- Target-only (the "??" skull on the level slot); getglobal returns nil for the -- player, guarded at use. frame.highLevel = getglobal(short .. "HighLevelTexture") -- Target-only (the level/name plate); getglobal returns nil for the player, guarded at use. frame.nameBackground = getglobal(name .. "NameBackground") -- The live model portrait (the real API's global, ref-UnitFrame.lua): bind the portrait -- region to this frame's unit token; the app renders that unit's model off-screen and feeds -- the bake back into the region (crates/benilla/src/portrait.rs). The binding is a token, so -- one call suffices — the app keeps the image current per token (it re-bakes on target / -- model change), which is why the ref's UNIT_PORTRAIT_UPDATE re-call isn't needed here (the -- event joins the surface when addon parity wants it). Until a bake lands (no unit / model -- still loading) the circle is simply empty. frame.portrait = getglobal(short .. "Portrait") SetPortraitTexture(frame.portrait, unit) -- The PvP flag icon (decision 0646), under the TextureFrame like the ring art it -- draws over — see BenillaUnitFrame_UpdatePvP. frame.pvpIcon = getglobal(short .. "PVPIcon") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_HEALTH") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MAXHEALTH") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_LEVEL") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_POWER_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MAXPOWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_DISPLAYPOWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_NAME_UPDATE") -- The PvP icon's repaint wire (decision 0646 §2) — in the reference exactly the three -- frames that draw the icon register it (PlayerFrame, TargetFrame, PartyMemberFrame) -- and nothing else does. frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_FACTION") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED") -- The aura rows and the classification border are target-only (ref TargetFrame_OnLoad -- registers UNIT_AURA and UNIT_CLASSIFICATION_CHANGED; PlayerFrame registers neither, -- and there is no CheckClassification for the player — your own frame never wears a -- dragon). The ring-art region is the one the border swap re-textures, so only the -- target caches the handle: its presence is what gates the swap in Update, the same -- nil-handle idiom highLevel/nameBackground use above. if unit == "target" then frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_AURA") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_CLASSIFICATION_CHANGED") frame.frameTexture = getglobal(name .. "Texture") end -- The portrait hit indicator (decision 0576): only the player frame registers -- UNIT_COMBAT in 1.12 (ref PlayerFrame_OnLoad — the target frame has no feedback -- text). Ref: CombatFeedback_Initialize(PlayerHitIndicator, 30). if unit == "player" then frame.feedbackText = getglobal(short .. Handles cached like pvpIcon above; their presence is what gates -- PlayerFrame_UpdateStatus in the shared Update. frame.statusTexture = getglobal(short .. Handle-gated in the -- shared Update exactly like statusTexture above — the target frame declares -- neither texture, so it never runs the law, and the party member frames run -- their own (PartyFrame.xml, a different predicate: an INDEX comparison). frame.leaderIcon = getglobal(short .. "LeaderIcon") frame.masterIcon = getglobal(short .. "MasterIcon") frame:RegisterEvent("PARTY_MEMBERS_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("PARTY_LEADER_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("PARTY_LOOT_METHOD_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("RAID_ROSTER_UPDATE") end -- A plain Frame isn't mouse-enabled by construction (only Button/EditBox are); enable it so -- the hover tooltip fires (the real client's unit frames take the mouse to target/tooltip). frame:EnableMouse(true) UnitFrame_Update() end
-- Hover: the engine's SetUnit — the byte-verified unit line law (decision 0276: name/ -- subtitle/level composition/PvP/Skinnable + the health bar), then the ref's reaction -- recolor of line 1 (ref UnitFrame_OnEnter l.68-76: the FrameXML half of the split). -- The plate goes to the DEFAULT corner, not beside the frame — ref UnitFrame_OnEnter -- l.56 is GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, this): unit-frame tooltips live at -- the screen's bottom-right like world hovers. (The TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME re-poll is not -- ours: the engine's health watcher is the live half of it, and name/level don't drift -- mid-hover yet.) -- -- The DETAILED-TOOLTIP FORK (ref UnitFrame_OnEnter l.58-67, director-approved 0663) is the -- surprising half: with tips on — 1.12's default, decision 0661 — the frame explains its -- RIGHT-CLICK MENU instead of the unit, and returns BEFORE SetUnit, so the health/level -- lines never render at all. Your own portrait always takes it; another player's takes it -- whenever they're your target. The ref excepts PartyMemberFrame1-4 by name; ours are a -- separate file with their own OnEnter (PartyFrame.xml), so there is nothing to except here. -- -- One divergence, named: the ref gates the second branch on UnitPlayerControlled("target"), -- which is true for a player OR a player's pet/charm. This engine has no such binding and no -- flag to build one from — UnitIsPlayer is the nearest honest read, so a charmed mob or -- another player's pet falls through to the unit tooltip where the reference would explain -- the menu. The player case, which is the one anybody hovers, is exact. -- ref UnitFrame_OnEnter l.55-57, ahead of everything else: the ONLY lit/grey cursor split -- over a UI element in 1.12, and it is authored here in Lua rather than in the engine -- (wow-re item-target-cursor-and-dropitemonunit.md 4.3). Bag and paper-doll slots have no -- such branch, which is why they show the ordinary pointer. -- A BAR's own hover (decision 1146; ref TextStatusBar's OnEnter/OnLeave on a mouse-enabled -- bar). Two jobs, and the second is the one a naive transcription drops: reveal the numbers -- while the pointer is on the bar, then hand the hover ON to the frame underneath, because -- a mouse-enabled child swallows the parent's OnEnter — and with it the unit tooltip AND -- the cast-cursor split that only exists over unit frames. Same for the click: the ref -- routes its bars' OnMouseUp straight back to the frame's own handler (PlayerFrame.xml -- l.304-306), which is what keeps a bar click targeting. -- -- `owner`/`ownerClick` are stamped at load rather than read from GetParent(), because the -- pet's bars are siblings of its TextureFrame, not children of the frame they belong to. function BenillaUnitFrameBar_OnEnter(bar) if TextStatusBar_UpdateTextString then TextStatusBar_UpdateTextString(bar) ShowTextStatusBarText(bar) end if bar.owner and BenillaUnitFrame_OnEnter and bar.owner.unit then BenillaUnitFrame_OnEnter(bar.owner) end end
function BenillaUnitFrameBar_OnLeave(bar) if HideTextStatusBarText then HideTextStatusBarText(bar) end if bar.owner and BenillaUnitFrame_OnLeave and bar.owner.unit then BenillaUnitFrame_OnLeave(bar.owner) end end
function BenillaUnitFrameBar_OnMouseUp(bar, button) if bar.ownerClick then bar.ownerClick(button) end end
-- The reference's names for the two unit-frame hover hooks, `this`-shaped, delegating to -- ours. `TipBuddy.lua:2770-2773` is the exact idiom this exists for: -- originalUnitFrame_OnEnter = UnitFrame_OnEnter -- function UnitFrame_OnEnter() originalUnitFrame_OnEnter() ... end -- Against a missing global that captured nil and raised on the first hover; against a -- RENAMED one it would have called ours with no frame. See ActionBar.xml for the full note. function UnitFrame_OnEnter() BenillaUnitFrame_OnEnter(this) end
function UnitFrame_OnLeave() BenillaUnitFrame_OnLeave(this) end
function BenillaUnitFrame_OnEnter(frame) local unit = frame.unit if SpellIsTargeting() then if SpellCanTargetUnit(unit) then SetCursor("CAST_CURSOR") else SetCursor("CAST_ERROR_CURSOR") end end if not UnitExists(unit) then return end GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, frame) if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS == "1" then if frame:GetName() == "PlayerFrame" then BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(frame, PARTY_OPTIONS_LABEL, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_PARTYOPTIONS) return elseif UnitIsPlayer("target") and not UnitIsUnit("target", "player") and not UnitIsUnit("target", "pet") then BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(frame, PLAYER_OPTIONS_LABEL, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, NEWBIE_TOOLTIP_PLAYEROPTIONS) return end end if GameTooltip:SetUnit(unit) then getglobal("GameTooltipTextLeft1"):SetTextColor(GameTooltip_UnitColor(unit)) end end
-- ref UnitFrame_OnLeave l.84-88: the fade is the tips-OFF branch. With detailed tips on the -- plate HIDES outright — the ref's own pairing, and the right one: an explanation that -- lingers on a ramp reads as a stuck tooltip, where a unit readout fading is the client's -- signature. (Items Hide, units fade — that split still holds for the world mouseover.) function BenillaUnitFrame_OnLeave(frame) -- ref UnitFrame_OnLeave l.86: leaving a unit frame while still targeting goes to the -- GREY cast cursor, not to the base one — you have left the only thing the armed spell -- could have bound. if SpellIsTargeting() then SetCursor("CAST_ERROR_CURSOR") end if SHOW_NEWBIE_TIPS == "1" then GameTooltip:Hide() else GameTooltip:FadeOut() end end
function UnitFrame_OnEvent(event) local frame = this -- UNIT_* events name their unit in arg1; ignore other units' updates. if string.sub(event, 1, 5) == "UNIT_" and arg1 ~= frame.unit then return end -- The hit-indicator feed (ref PlayerFrame_OnEvent's UNIT_COMBAT arm): no repaint — -- the event carries feedback, not state. if event == "UNIT_COMBAT" then CombatFeedback_OnCombatEvent(frame, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5) return end -- The status flash's state arms (ref PlayerFrame_OnEvent l.100-115, decision 1082): -- inCombat = auto-attack active, onHateList = on something's aggro list; a world -- entry resets both (the ref's own PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD arm). The repaint itself -- rides the shared Update below — this file's posture (the PvP sound note). if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" then frame.inCombat = nil frame.onHateList = nil elseif event == "PLAYER_ENTER_COMBAT" then frame.inCombat = 1 elseif event == "PLAYER_LEAVE_COMBAT" then frame.inCombat = nil elseif event == "PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED" then frame.onHateList = 1 elseif event == "PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED" then frame.onHateList = nil end UnitFrame_Update() -- The player's flag-change sound (decision 0646 §2/§4). The reference plays -- igPVPUpdate inside PlayerFrame_UpdatePvPStatus's two show branches, which it only -- ever reaches from UNIT_FACTION; our repaint runs from the shared Update on every -- event, so the sound rides the (edge-fired) event instead of the repaint — one -- sound per real flag change, which is what the reference audibly does. if event == "UNIT_FACTION" and frame.unit == "player" and frame.pvpShown then PlaySound("igPVPUpdate") end end
-- The PvP flag icon (decision 0646 §4). The reference writes this law twice with -- identical branches — PlayerFrame_UpdatePvPStatus (ref-PlayerFrame.lua l.55-79) and the -- tail of TargetFrame_CheckFaction (ref-TargetFrame.lua l.193-202) — so it lives once -- here. Branch ORDER is the reference's and it is load-bearing: free-for-all wins -- outright (an FFA-flagged player shows the FFA skull even while ordinarily flagged), and -- the faction leg needs BOTH a resolvable side and the flag. `frame.pvpShown` is what the -- caller sounds off. function BenillaUnitFrame_UpdatePvP(frame) local icon = frame.pvpIcon if not icon then return end local unit = frame.unit local texture if UnitIsPVPFreeForAll(unit) then texture = "Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-PVP-FFA" else local factionGroup = UnitFactionGroup(unit) if factionGroup and UnitIsPVP(unit) then texture = "Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-PVP-" .. factionGroup end end frame.pvpShown = texture ~= nil if texture then icon:SetTexture(texture) icon:Show() else icon:Hide() end end
-- ── Combat feedback: the portrait hit indicator (decision 0576) ────────────────────── -- Our implementation of what ref CombatFeedback.lua specifies, on frame-param style (the -- ref reads `this`). Timings, colors and size factors are its MEASURED values. The words -- come from the GLOBALS, exactly as the ref builds this table (CombatFeedback.lua l.6-17: -- CombatFeedbackText["MISS"] = TEXT(MISS)), so a localized install shows its own — the app -- runs the real GlobalStrings.lua off the patch chain before this file (ui_script/mod.rs). -- The enUS literals are the fallback for the test harnesses, which load no patch chain. COMBATFEEDBACK_FADEINTIME = 0.2 COMBATFEEDBACK_HOLDTIME = 0.7 COMBATFEEDBACK_FADEOUTTIME = 0.3
CombatFeedbackText = { INTERRUPT = INTERRUPT or "Interrupt", MISS = MISS or "Miss", RESIST = RESIST or "Resist", DODGE = DODGE or "Dodge", PARRY = PARRY or "Parry", BLOCK = BLOCK or "Block", EVADE = EVADE or "Evade", IMMUNE = IMMUNE or "Immune", DEFLECT = DEFLECT or "Deflect", ABSORB = ABSORB or "Absorb", REFLECT = REFLECT or "Reflect", }
-- The indicator says one of two things: a NUMBER, when something moved a bar, or a WORD, -- when nothing did. Everything below is that split. `scale` is a multiple of the frame's -- own indicator height — 1 is "as authored" — and the multiples themselves are the -- reference's measurements: half again for a big hit, three quarters for one that was -- stopped, half for one that could never land.
-- The two events that move a bar the friendly way, and the colour each prints in. (A -- WOUND prints a number too, but its colour depends on the school, so it is settled in -- place below.) local COMBAT_FEEDBACK_GAIN = { HEAL = { r = 0.0, g = 1.0, b = 0.0 }, ENERGIZE = { r = 0.41, g = 0.8, b = 0.94 }, }
-- The words that do not print at the indicator's authored height. Everything else does. local COMBAT_FEEDBACK_WORD_SCALE = { IMMUNE = 0.5, BLOCK = 0.75, }
-- A wound that did no damage was stopped by one of three things, and in each case the -- flag naming it is also the key of the word for it. Anything else was a plain miss. local COMBAT_FEEDBACK_SOAKED = { ABSORB = 1, BLOCK = 1, RESIST = 1 }
-- What a zero-damage wound reads as: the word, and the size it prints at. Being stopped -- reads small; missing outright reads full size, because a miss is the ordinary case. local function CombatFeedback_Stopped(flags) if COMBAT_FEEDBACK_SOAKED[flags] then return CombatFeedbackText[flags], 0.75 end return CombatFeedbackText["MISS"], 1.0 end
-- The size a landed blow reads at. A crushing blow is as loud as a critical; a glancing -- one is as quiet as a soak. local function CombatFeedback_HitScale(flags) if flags == "CRITICAL" or flags == "CRUSHING" then return 1.5 elseif flags == "GLANCING" then return 0.75 end return 1.0 end
function CombatFeedback_OnCombatEvent(frame, event, flags, amount, type) local feedbackText = frame.feedbackText if not feedbackText then return end
-- The default reading, which most events take unchanged: this event's own word, at the -- authored height, in white. An event with no word at all prints nothing, which is the -- honest thing to do with a feedback kind we do not have a string for. local text = CombatFeedbackText[event] local scale = 1.0 local r, g, b = 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
if event == "WOUND" then if amount == 0 then text, scale = CombatFeedback_Stopped(flags) else text = amount scale = CombatFeedback_HitScale(flags) -- A non-zero school means a spell landed it: spell damage prints yellow where -- a physical hit prints white. if type > 0 then r, g, b = 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 end end else local gain = COMBAT_FEEDBACK_GAIN[event] if gain then text = amount r, g, b = gain.r, gain.g, gain.b -- A critical heal or power gain reads big. Note this is the ONLY flag that -- resizes one — a wound's crushing/glancing legs do not apply here. if flags == "CRITICAL" then scale = 1.5 end else scale = COMBAT_FEEDBACK_WORD_SCALE[event] or 1.0 end end
frame.feedbackStartTime = GetTime()
feedbackText:SetTextHeight(frame.feedbackFontHeight * scale) feedbackText:SetText(text) feedbackText:SetTextColor(r, g, b) feedbackText:SetAlpha(0.0) feedbackText:Show() end
-- The fade envelope (ref CombatFeedback_OnUpdate): 0.2 s ramp in, 0.7 s hold, 0.3 s -- ramp out, then Hide. GetTime-based like the ref — no per-tick accumulation. function CombatFeedback_OnUpdate(frame) local feedbackText = frame.feedbackText if not (feedbackText and feedbackText:IsVisible()) then return end local elapsedTime = GetTime() - frame.feedbackStartTime local fadeInTime = COMBATFEEDBACK_FADEINTIME if elapsedTime < fadeInTime then feedbackText:SetAlpha(elapsedTime / fadeInTime) return end local holdTime = COMBATFEEDBACK_HOLDTIME if elapsedTime < fadeInTime + holdTime then feedbackText:SetAlpha(1.0) return end local fadeOutTime = COMBATFEEDBACK_FADEOUTTIME if elapsedTime < fadeInTime + holdTime + fadeOutTime then feedbackText:SetAlpha(1.0 - (elapsedTime - holdTime - fadeInTime) / fadeOutTime) return end feedbackText:Hide() end
-- Pull the unit's current state and repaint. A non-existent unit hides the whole frame. -- The classification border art (TargetFrame_CheckClassification, ref-TargetFrame.lua -- l.205-218) — re-expressed branch for branch, and the shape is the surprise: 1.12 has FIVE -- classifications but only THREE border textures, because elite, rareelite and worldboss all -- take the same Elite art. There is no rare-elite border in this build and no rare-elite -- tooltip word either (the level line's rank table is {"", ELITE, ELITE, BOSS, ""}), so -- "rareelite" is a distinction the API makes and the pixels never do. Verified rather than -- assumed, because later expansions DO ship UI-TargetingFrame-Rare-Elite and it would be the -- natural thing to write: that path is absent from 1.12's patch chain entirely, and the ref -- Lua sends rareelite to the Elite art. -- -- SetTexture is the whole operation — no TexCoords, size or anchor changes. That is only -- sound because all three BLPs are 256x128 (checked, not assumed), so the region's -- XML-declared TexCoords (0.09375..1.0 x 0..0.78125 = the 232x100 crop) frame all three -- identically, and our SetTexture touches only the path (it leaves tex_coords alone). function TargetFrame_CheckClassification() local frame = this local classification = UnitClassification(frame.unit) if classification == "worldboss" or classification == "rareelite" or classification == "elite" then frame.frameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-TargetingFrame-Elite") elseif classification == "rare" then frame.frameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-TargetingFrame-Rare") else frame.frameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-TargetingFrame") end end
-- ── One unit's two bars, from its token ─────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Three frames in this file paint exactly this, and until 1576 each wrote it out: the -- health bar's range and value, then the power bar's colour off BENILLA_POWER_COLORS and -- its own range and value — or no power bar at all, this file's convention for a unit with -- no resource. Returns whether the unit HAS one, which is what the pet frame swaps its -- plate on (the reference has no such art for the others and leaves an empty rail drawn). -- -- The bars are ARGUMENTS rather than fields: the player and target frames call theirs -- `manabar` and the pet frame calls its `manabar`, following the reference's own two names -- for one rail, and a helper that reached for a field would have to pick a side. -- -- NO label on the power bar. 1.12 names the resource there (ref UnitFrame_UpdateManaType -- l.129 → "Rage 0 / 100" off ManaBarColor's own prefix field, and CharacterFrame_OnLoad -- labels health and XP the same way). Shipped in 1146, cut on the director's call the same -- day: bare numbers read better on these bars (decision 1147). The mechanism stays — -- SetTextStatusBarTextPrefix is live and one call brings any label back — only the calls -- are gone. function BenillaUnitFrame_PaintBars(healthbar, manabar, unit) healthbar:SetMinMaxValues(0, UnitHealthMax(unit)) healthbar:SetValue(UnitHealth(unit)) local maxPower = UnitManaMax(unit) if maxPower <= 0 then manabar:Hide() return false end manabar:Show() local _, powerToken = UnitPowerType(unit) local swatch = BENILLA_POWER_COLORS[powerToken] or BENILLA_POWER_COLORS.MANA manabar:SetStatusBarColor(swatch.r, swatch.g, swatch.b) manabar:SetMinMaxValues(0, maxPower) manabar:SetValue(UnitMana(unit)) return true end

-- The level slot (TargetFrame_CheckLevel, ref-TargetFrame.lua l.119-142): a corpse -- target or one whose level "can't be told" (UnitLevel ≤ 0 — the −1 return for a -- world boss / a hostile 10+ levels up) shows the skull instead of the number; a -- told level is difficulty-colored when the target is attackable (GetDifficultyColor, -- the same con law the V-plate paints its level with) and plain gold when not. -- The player frame has no skull region and shows its own level, always gold. local level = UnitLevel(unit) if frame.highLevel then if UnitIsCorpse(unit) or level <= 0 then frame.levelText:Hide() frame.highLevel:Show() else frame.levelText:SetText(level) if UnitCanAttack("player", unit) then local color = GetDifficultyColor(level) frame.levelText:SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) else frame.levelText:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.82, 0.0) end frame.levelText:Show() frame.highLevel:Hide() end else frame.levelText:SetText(level) end

A PLAYER-CONTROLLED target takes the player branch (l.145-174); only an NPC -- takes the reaction swatch (l.179-190): the resolved UnitReactionColor (neutral → -- yellow), or blue when the reaction can't be told (nil) — a player never reads the -- reaction green, which is why the two paths differ at all. -- The player branch runs the ref's full ladder now that the -- PvP wire carries it (decision 0646 §4): hostile red, else attackable-but-not-hostile -- yellow (l.158), else "we can assist them but they're PvP-flagged" green (l.163), else -- blue. Only the tapped-by-other grey (l.176) is still deferred — it needs the tap wire. -- The ref's first leg tests mutual attackability (UnitCanAttack both ways); our -- UnitCanAttack carries only the player→unit direction, so UnitIsEnemy (reaction ≤ 2) -- stands in for it — the same substitution this branch has always made. (The ref gates on -- UnitPlayerControlled, which also covers pets; UnitIsPlayer is the player half we can -- resolve — see the header deviation.) if frame.nameBackground then if UnitIsPlayer(unit) then local c if UnitIsEnemy(unit, "player") then c = BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS[2] elseif UnitCanAttack("player", unit) then c = BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS[4] elseif UnitIsPVP(unit) then c = BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS[6] end if c then frame.nameBackground:SetVertexColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) else frame.nameBackground:SetVertexColor(0.0, 0.0, 1.0) end else local reaction = UnitReaction(unit, "player") local c = reaction and BENILLA_REACTION_COLORS[reaction] if c then frame.nameBackground:SetVertexColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) else frame.nameBackground:SetVertexColor(0.0, 0.0, 1.0) end end end

This site used to SetText("DEAD") a -- LITERAL and blank it when alive, which put the KEY on screen in caps — `DEAD` is a -- GlobalStrings key (l.898 = "Dead"), not the string, and typing a key as display text -- is the "CREATE_MACROS" failure of 0983/0991 again. Nothing here names the word now: -- it comes from the FontString's `text="DEAD"` attribute, which the loader resolves -- through the global (loader/mod.rs resolve_text), locale and all. -- -- `UnitIsConnected` is the reference's own second term and is what tells dead from -- LINK-dead: a disconnected player reads 0 health here and is not dead. The ToT twin -- (TargetofTarget_CheckDead) has carried it since it was written; this leg had not. if frame.deadText then if UnitHealth(unit) <= 0 and UnitIsConnected(unit) then frame.deadText:Show() else frame.deadText:Hide() end end

Only called with a live target (UnitFrame_Update guards). -- DebuffTypeColor is defined by BuffFrame.xml, which loads AFTER this file — safe, because -- this function only runs on events, never at load (no target exists at load). function BenillaTargetAuras_Update() local button local numBuffs = 0 for i = 1, MAX_TARGET_BUFFS do local name, icon = UnitBuff("target", i) button = getglobal("TargetFrameBuff" .. i) if name then getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon"):SetTexture(icon or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) local color = DebuffTypeColor[debuffType] or DebuffTypeColor["none"] local countText = getglobal(button:GetName() .. Both legs are the reference's, and both are live now that the frame exists. local targetofTarget = TargetofTargetFrame:IsShown() local debuffWrap = 6 if targetofTarget then debuffWrap = 5 end
if UnitIsFriend("player", "target") then TargetFrameBuff1:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "TargetFrame", "BOTTOMLEFT", 5, 32) TargetFrameDebuff1:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "TargetFrameBuff1", "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -2) else TargetFrameDebuff1:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", "TargetFrame", "BOTTOMLEFT", 5, 32) if targetofTarget then -- ref l.318-326 writes this as THREE branches (< 5, 5..9, >= 10) whose first -- two are character-for-character identical; the buffs open under the second -- debuff row until there is a third. "Border") border:SetWidth(debuffFrameSize) border:SetHeight(debuffFrameSize) button:SetWidth(debuffSize) button:SetHeight(debuffSize) end

-- The aura hover (ref TargetDebuffButtonTemplate/TargetBuffButtonTemplate OnEnter, -- l.60-62/l.79-81): the aura tooltip, seated BOTTOMRIGHT of the button. function BenillaTargetAuraButton_OnEnter(button, harmful) if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_BOTTOMRIGHT", 15, -25) if harmful then GameTooltip:SetUnitDebuff("target", button:GetID()) else GameTooltip:SetUnitBuff("target", button:GetID()) end end
-- The status flash's paint (ref PlayerFrame_UpdateStatus, re-expressed onto frame-param -- style; decision 1082). Priority is the ref's: RESTING wins over combat — sitting in an -- inn mid-auto-attack shows the zzz — then the auto-attack state (gold ring/zzz vs red -- ring/swords/red disc), then bare swords for on-someone's-aggro-list, then nothing. function PlayerFrame_UpdateStatus() local frame = this if IsResting() then frame.statusTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.88, 0.25, 1.0) frame.statusTexture:Show() frame.restIcon:Show() frame.attackIcon:Hide() frame.restGlow:Show() frame.attackGlow:Hide() frame.statusGlow:Show() frame.attackBackground:Hide() elseif frame.inCombat then frame.statusTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0) frame.statusTexture:Show() frame.attackIcon:Show() frame.restIcon:Hide() frame.attackGlow:Show() frame.restGlow:Hide() frame.statusGlow:Show() frame.attackBackground:Show() elseif frame.onHateList then frame.attackIcon:Show() frame.restIcon:Hide() frame.statusGlow:Hide() frame.attackBackground:Hide() else frame.statusTexture:Hide() frame.restIcon:Hide() frame.attackIcon:Hide() frame.statusGlow:Hide() frame.attackBackground:Hide() end end
-- The leader / master-looter icons on the player's own frame (ref -- PlayerFrame_UpdatePartyLeader, re-expressed onto frame-param style; report B317). -- -- Two DIFFERENT predicates, and the asymmetry is the reference's own. The leader icon asks -- IsPartyLeader() — a boolean about us — where the member frames ask whether the leader -- INDEX equals their id, because the player has no index on that scale (0 is "the player -- leads", not "party0"). The master icon then asks whether GetLootMethod's second return -- is 0, which is that same scale reading "the player is master looter"; the group test -- beside it is the reference's own guard, and it is not redundant with ours — a solo -- player's master_looter is None, so `masterId == 0` is already false, but reproducing the -- expression keeps us honest if that ever stops being true. function BenillaPlayerFrame_UpdatePartyLeader(frame) if IsPartyLeader() then frame.leaderIcon:Show() else frame.leaderIcon:Hide() end local lootMethod, masterId = GetLootMethod() if masterId == 0 and (GetNumPartyMembers() > 0 or GetNumRaidMembers() > 0) then frame.masterIcon:Show() else frame.masterIcon:Hide() end end
-- ref PlayerFrame_OnUpdate: the status pulse — a 0.5 s triangle wave between alpha -- 55/255 and 255/255 on the ADD-blend status ring and the icon glow, run only while the -- ring is visible (resting or auto-attacking); the hit-indicator fade rides the same -- tick, exactly as before. function PlayerFrame_OnUpdate(elapsed) local frame = this if frame.statusTexture:IsVisible() then local counter = frame.statusCounter + elapsed local sign = frame.statusSign if counter > 0.5 then sign = -sign frame.statusSign = sign end counter = mod(counter, 0.5) frame.statusCounter = counter local alpha if sign == 1 then alpha = (55 + counter * 400) / 255 else alpha = (255 - counter * 400) / 255 end frame.statusTexture:SetAlpha(alpha) frame.statusGlow:SetAlpha(alpha) end CombatFeedback_OnUpdate(frame) end
-- Left-click the player frame to target yourself (ref PlayerFrame_OnClick, the LeftButton -- branch: an item on the cursor auto-equips, otherwise TargetUnit("player")); right-click -- opens the SELF menu (ref's ToggleDropDownMenu at (106, 27), decision 0434 phase 5). The -- ref's frame is a Button; ours is a mouse-enabled Frame, which fires OnClick on release -- with arg1 = the button. The self-target itself is the byte-verified way the client -- selects its own unit; the world-model click is a separate path, deliberately left out -- (director's call). function PlayerFrame_OnClick(button) if button == "RightButton" then ToggleDropDownMenu(1, nil, PlayerFrameDropDown, "PlayerFrame", 106, 27) return end if button ~= "LeftButton" then return end if CursorHasItem() then AutoEquipCursorItem() else TargetUnit("player") end end

The menu pick is the ref's law: self → SELF, -- party member → PARTY, other player → PLAYER, NPC → the bare raid-target icon list. function TargetFrameDropDown_OnLoad() UIDropDownMenu_Initialize(this, TargetFrameDropDown_Initialize, "MENU") end

Most specific first: -- yourself → SELF -- your own pet → PET. Selecting your pet and right-clicking the TARGET -- frame is still the pet's menu; the ref's own second -- branch (TargetFrame.lua l.440-441), which sat as a -- comment here until the "pet" token (0990) and then the -- menu itself (1066). -- anything that is not a player → an NPC, which gets only the raid-mark list -- a player, in your party or not → PARTY / PLAYER local function TargetFrameMenu() if UnitIsUnit("target", "player") then return "SELF" end if UnitIsUnit("target", "pet") then return "PET" end if not UnitIsPlayer("target") then return "RAID_TARGET_ICON", RAID_TARGET_ICON end if UnitInParty("target") then return "PARTY" end return "PLAYER" end

-- The two saved settings (ref UIOptionsFrame.lua l.116-119), with the reference's own -- defaults: the frame ships OFF, and its mode ships at "always". They are saved-variable -- globals rather than CVars because that is what they are in 1.12 — the Interface panel's -- `uvar` store (OptionsFrame.xml's three-store note), and RegisterForSave is what persists -- them into benilla-config (saved.rs). SHOW_TARGET_OF_TARGET = "0" RegisterForSave("SHOW_TARGET_OF_TARGET") SHOW_TARGET_OF_TARGET_STATE = "5" RegisterForSave("SHOW_TARGET_OF_TARGET_STATE")
-- Does the group state allow the frame right now? The five modes, in the reference's own -- numbering (its dropdown writes these strings, and OPTION_TOOLTIP_TARGETOFTARGET1..5 -- describes them in this order): 1 raid, 2 party, 3 solo, 4 party or raid, 5 always. -- Written as a predicate rather than the reference's if/elseif ladder — see the DEVIATIONS -- note above for the leaked state that ladder has in its solo leg. LOCAL: the reference has -- no such function, and inventing a global for it would put a name in `_G` that no addon -- written against 1.12 can expect (the `Benilla*` prefix is for the ones we must expose). local function TargetofTarget_ModeAllows() local mode = SHOW_TARGET_OF_TARGET_STATE local raid = GetNumRaidMembers() local party = GetNumPartyMembers() if mode == "1" then return raid > 0 end if mode == "2" then return party > 0 and raid == 0 end if mode == "3" then return raid == 0 and party == 0 end if mode == "4" then return raid > 0 or party > 0 end if mode == "5" then return true end return false end
-- The visibility law + the repaint (ref TargetofTarget_Update, l.503-541). Four gates -- besides the switch and the mode, all the reference's: there must BE a target, it must -- have a target, it must not be YOU (your own target's target is your own target — the -- frame would restate the frame it hangs off), and it must be alive. function TargetofTarget_Update() local frame = TargetofTargetFrame local was = frame:IsShown() local show = SHOW_TARGET_OF_TARGET == "1" and UnitExists("target") and UnitExists("targettarget") and not UnitIsUnit("player", "target") and UnitHealth("target") > 0 and TargetofTarget_ModeAllows() if show then frame:Show() BenillaUnitFrame_PaintBars(frame.healthbar, frame.manabar, "targettarget") TargetofTargetName:SetText(UnitName("targettarget") or "") TargetofTarget_CheckDead() -- The reference's own line (l.536), and it is not redundant with the health -- check's tint: that one only ever touches a PLAYER's portrait, so a creature -- inherits whatever alpha the last player left behind without this. TargetofTargetPortrait:SetAlpha(1.0) BenillaTargetofTarget_UpdateDebuffs() else frame:Hide() end -- The target's OWN aura rows wrap at 5 instead of 6 while this frame stands beside -- them (BenillaTargetAuras_Update), so a change of shown state re-lays them out. The -- reference re-runs them on the SHOW leg only (l.534) and never on the hide, which -- leaves the rows wrapped short after the frame goes away. if frame:IsShown() ~= was and UnitExists("target") then BenillaTargetAuras_Update() end end
-- ref TargetofTarget_CheckDead (l.559-567): the DEAD word over a dimmed trough. The -- connected test is the reference's and it is what tells "dead" from "linkdead" — -- a disconnected player reads 0 health here and is not dead. function TargetofTarget_CheckDead() local down = UnitHealth("targettarget") <= 0 and UnitIsConnected("targettarget") TargetofTargetBackground:SetAlpha(down and 0.9 or 1) if down then TargetofTargetDeadText:Show() else TargetofTargetDeadText:Hide() end end
-- The four readings a PLAYER's portrait can carry here (ref TargetofTargetHealthCheck's -- own four SetVertexColor calls, l.573-583): a corpse greys, a released ghost goes blue, -- a fifth of health or less runs red, and anything else is untinted. local TOT_PORTRAIT_TINT = { dead = { r = 0.35, g = 0.35, b = 0.35 }, ghost = { r = 0.2, g = 0.2, b = 0.75 }, hurt = { r = 1.0, g = 0.0, b = 0.0 }, alive = { r = 1.0, g = 1.0, b = 1.0 }, }
-- ref TargetofTargetHealthCheck (l.569-585), the health bar's OnValueChanged: the -- portrait tints with the unit's state — grey dead, blue ghost, red under a fifth of its -- health, white otherwise. PLAYERS ONLY, which is the reference's gate and not an -- oversight: a creature's portrait carries no such reading anywhere in 1.12. function TargetofTargetHealthCheck() if not UnitIsPlayer("targettarget") then return end local bar = this local _, maxHP = bar:GetMinMaxValues() local percent = 0 if maxHP > 0 then percent = bar:GetValue() / maxHP end bar:GetParent().unitHPPercent = percent -- The reading, then one paint. Priority is the reference's ladder: dead outranks -- ghost outranks hurt, and anything else is untinted. local tint = TOT_PORTRAIT_TINT.alive if UnitIsDead("targettarget") then tint = TOT_PORTRAIT_TINT.dead elseif UnitIsGhost("targettarget") then tint = TOT_PORTRAIT_TINT.ghost elseif percent > 0 and percent <= 0.2 then tint = TOT_PORTRAIT_TINT.hurt end TargetofTargetPortrait:SetVertexColor(tint.r, tint.g, tint.b, 1.0) end
-- The four debuff buttons (ref calls RefreshBuffs(this, 0, "targettarget"), BuffFrame.lua -- l.262-312, over MAX_PARTY_DEBUFFS = 4). Same shape as the pet frame's row, plus the -- dispel tint the party/pet rows do not carry — RefreshBuffs colours its border by -- debuffType exactly as the target frame's row does. function BenillaTargetofTarget_UpdateDebuffs() for i = 1, 4 do local button = getglobal("TargetofTargetFrameDebuff" .. i) local _, icon, _, debuffType = UnitDebuff("targettarget", i) if icon then getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon"):SetTexture(icon) local color = DebuffTypeColor[debuffType] or DebuffTypeColor["none"] getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Border"):SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) button:Show() else button:Hide() end end end
function TargetofTarget_OnLoad() local frame = this frame.unit = "targettarget" frame.healthbar = TargetofTargetHealthBar frame.manabar = TargetofTargetManaBar -- The recessed-bar look, the same mechanism every frame in this file uses (decision -- 0884): the bars one frame level BELOW the art's TextureFrame, because the draw layer -- is bucket-wide and the frame level is the one key term above it. The reference -- spends its level the other way round (RaiseFrameLevel on the TextureFrame); same -- ordering, and ours matches its siblings here. local level = TargetofTargetTextureFrame:GetFrameLevel() frame.healthbar:SetFrameLevel(level - 1) frame.manabar:SetFrameLevel(level - 1) -- The live model portrait, bound once by token (see BenillaUnitFrame_OnLoad's note): -- the app keeps this slot's bake current, and it only bakes at all while this frame is -- on screen (portrait/mod.rs's `"targettarget"` arm). SetPortraitTexture(TargetofTargetPortrait, "targettarget") -- Every event the shown frame's paint reads. The `"target"` half is not incidental: -- the visibility law gates on the TARGET being alive, so the target's own health has -- to reach this frame too. for _, wire in ipairs({ "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD", "PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED", "PARTY_MEMBERS_CHANGED", "RAID_ROSTER_UPDATE", "UNIT_HEALTH", "UNIT_MAXHEALTH", "UNIT_POWER_UPDATE", "UNIT_MAXPOWER", "UNIT_DISPLAYPOWER", "UNIT_NAME_UPDATE", "UNIT_AURA", }) do frame:RegisterEvent(wire) end frame:EnableMouse(true) TargetofTarget_Update() end
-- Every UNIT_* event this frame registers names a unit in arg1, and exactly two of them -- concern it: its own, and the target whose health gates its visibility. Everything else -- (a party member's tick, the player's own) is somebody else's update. function TargetofTarget_OnEvent(event) if string.sub(event, 1, 5) == "UNIT_" and arg1 ~= "targettarget" and arg1 ~= "target" then return end TargetofTarget_Update() end
-- ref TargetofTarget_OnClick (l.543-557). function TargetofTarget_OnClick(button) local armed = SpellIsTargeting() if button ~= "LeftButton" then -- Right-click cancels an armed spell and does nothing else: unlike the player, -- target and pet frames, this one has no unit menu in the reference. if armed and button == "RightButton" then SpellStopTargeting() end return end -- Most specific first, the pet frame's order: an armed spell binds to the unit, then -- a held item drops on it, and with an empty cursor the click SELECTS it — which is -- the whole point of the frame, and the one leg the target frame's click does not have. if armed then SpellTargetUnit("targettarget") return end if CursorHasItem() then DropItemOnUnit("targettarget") return end TargetUnit("targettarget") end
-- ref TargetFrame_OnUpdate (l.256-260) — the one thing the event feed cannot carry. A -- token that goes away is CLEARED, not announced (ui_unit.rs: "clearing a token isn't a -- UNIT_* event"), so this reconciles the frame's shown state against the token's existence -- once per frame. It runs only while the target frame itself is shown, which is only while -- you have a target — the cost is one compare, and it is the reference's own line. -- Both sides are normalised to booleans on purpose. They happen to agree today (a frame's -- IsShown answers true/false, and so does UnitExists), but a REGION's IsShown answers the -- 1.12 shape of 1/nil, and the day UnitExists is moved onto it a bare `~=` here would be -- true forever — a silent per-frame full repaint, which is the one thing this line exists -- to avoid. function TargetFrame_OnUpdate() local shown = TargetofTargetFrame:IsShown() and true or false local exists = UnitExists("targettarget") and true or false if shown ~= exists then TargetofTarget_Update() end end

function PetFrame_OnLoad() local frame = this frame.portrait = PetPortrait frame.healthbar = PetFrameHealthBar frame.manabar = PetFrameManaBar frame.nameText = PetName -- The recessed-bar look, the same mechanism the player/target/party frames use -- (decision 0884): push the bars one frame level BELOW the art's TextureFrame, because -- the draw layer is bucket-wide and the frame level is the one key term above it. local level = PetFrameTextureFrame:GetFrameLevel() frame.healthbar:SetFrameLevel(level - 1) frame.manabar:SetFrameLevel(level - 1) -- The pet's numerals, textLockable like the ref's (PetFrame.xml l.139/164; 1143). if TextStatusBar_Initialize then -- engine tests load file subsets TextStatusBar_Initialize(frame.healthbar) TextStatusBar_Initialize(frame.manabar) SetTextStatusBarText(frame.healthbar, PetFrameHealthBarText) SetTextStatusBarText(frame.manabar, PetFrameManaBarText) frame.healthbar.textLockable = 1 frame.manabar.textLockable = 1 end -- The pet's bars hover for their numbers, but hand nothing on: the pet frame has no -- OnEnter of its own, and its click is its own handler (1146). frame.healthbar.ownerClick = PetFrame_OnClick frame.manabar.ownerClick = PetFrame_OnClick frame.attackModeCounter = 0 frame.attackModeSign = -1 frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_PET") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_AURA") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_HEALTH") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MAXHEALTH") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_POWER_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_MAXPOWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_DISPLAYPOWER") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_NAME_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("PET_ATTACK_START") frame:RegisterEvent("PET_ATTACK_STOP") frame:RegisterEvent("UNIT_HAPPINESS") frame:EnableMouse(true) PetFrame_Update() end
-- ref PetFrame_OnEvent, with both of its argument gates kept: UNIT_PET names the OWNER -- ("player" — wow-re §9 carves the arg), every other UNIT_* names the pet itself. Getting -- those backwards is how a pet frame ends up repainting off the player's health. function PetFrame_OnEvent(event) local frame = this if event == "PET_ATTACK_START" then PetAttackModeTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) PetAttackModeTexture:Show() return elseif event == "PET_ATTACK_STOP" then PetAttackModeTexture:Hide() return elseif event == "UNIT_HAPPINESS" then -- The ref's own last arm: repaint the icon alone, not the whole frame. PetFrame_SetHappiness() return elseif event == "UNIT_PET" then if arg1 ~= "player" then return end elseif string.sub(event, 1, 5) == "UNIT_" and arg1 ~= "pet" then return end PetFrame_Update() end
function PetFrame_Update() local frame = this if not UnitExists("pet") then frame:Hide() return end frame:Show() SetPortraitTexture(frame.portrait, "pet") frame.nameText:SetText(UnitName("pet") or "")
-- The ref's art swap (PetFrame.lua's Update): a powerless pet wears the -NoMana plate, -- which has no mana rail to leave empty. Which plate is exactly the shared paint's -- return — the pet is the only frame here whose art carries that distinction. if BenillaUnitFrame_PaintBars(frame.healthbar, frame.manabar, "pet") then PetFrameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-SmallTargetingFrame") else PetFrameTexture:SetTexture("Interface\\TargetingFrame\\UI-SmallTargetingFrame-NoMana") end
BenillaPetFrame_UpdateDebuffs() PetFrame_SetHappiness() end
-- ── The happiness face (decision 1005; ref PetFrame_SetHappiness, PetFrame.lua l.132-156) -- -- `Interface\PetPaperDollFrame\UI-PetHappiness` is one row of three faces, and each cut is -- a MEASURED value off that file. The buckets run RIGHT to left across the strip — bucket -- 1 (unhappy) takes the rightmost cut and bucket 3 (happy) sits at x=0 — which is why the -- left edges below descend as the index climbs. A bucket outside 1..3 selects no cell at -- all and the icon keeps whatever face it was already wearing, deliberately: see the note -- on bucket 0 below. local PET_HAPPINESS_CELL = { { 0.375, 0.5625, 0, 0.359375 }, { 0.1875, 0.375, 0, 0.359375 }, { 0, 0.1875, 0, 0.359375 }, }
-- `GetPetHappiness` hands back a PRE-BUCKETED 1/2/3 — the client does the thresholding -- against PetPersonality.dbc, not this function — plus the two numbers that bucket -- selects. Three things here are load-bearing and each is the reference's own: -- * the hide test is on the bucket being ABSENT, not on it being zero, so a bucket of -- **0** (truthy in Lua) leaves the icon SHOWING with whatever texcoords it had. -- Testing `happiness == 0` or coercing 0 to nil would hide a frame the reference shows. -- * only a HUNTER's pet has a face at all — `HasPetUI`'s second return is the whole gate, -- and its first return is nothing to do with this frame. -- * the loyalty line is chosen by the SIGN of loyaltyRate, which is why that return is -- unscaled and allowed to be negative. Exactly zero means "steady", and says nothing. function PetFrame_SetHappiness() local happiness, damagePercentage, loyaltyRate = GetPetHappiness() local _, isHunterPet = HasPetUI() if not (happiness and isHunterPet) then PetFrameHappiness:Hide() return end PetFrameHappiness:Show()
local cell = PET_HAPPINESS_CELL[happiness] if cell then PetFrameHappinessTexture:SetTexCoord(cell[1], cell[2], cell[3], cell[4]) end
PetFrameHappiness.tooltip = getglobal("PET_HAPPINESS" .. happiness) PetFrameHappiness.tooltipDamage = format(PET_DAMAGE_PERCENTAGE, damagePercentage) if loyaltyRate < 0 then PetFrameHappiness.tooltipLoyalty = getglobal("LOSING_LOYALTY") elseif loyaltyRate > 0 then PetFrameHappiness.tooltipLoyalty = getglobal("GAINING_LOYALTY") else PetFrameHappiness.tooltipLoyalty = nil end end
-- The happiness face's hover. Both extra lines are drawn the same way — plain white, -- nothing in the right-hand column — and either can be absent, so the stanza is written -- once. The whole tooltip waits on the headline: until SetHappiness has run there is -- nothing to say, and an empty plate is worse than none. local function AddHappinessTooltipLine(text) if text then GameTooltip:AddLine(text, "", 1, 1, 1) end end
function BenillaPetHappiness_OnEnter(frame) if not frame.tooltip then return end GameTooltip:SetOwner(frame, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") GameTooltip:SetText(frame.tooltip) AddHappinessTooltipLine(frame.tooltipDamage) AddHappinessTooltipLine(frame.tooltipLoyalty) GameTooltip:Show() end
-- The four debuff buttons (ref PetFrame.xml's $parentDebuff1..4 over RefreshBuffs). The pet -- carries no aura timers — no unit but yourself does on the 1.12 wire (decision 0257 B6) — -- so these are icon + border + stack count, the party rows' shape exactly. function BenillaPetFrame_UpdateDebuffs() for i = 1, 4 do local button = getglobal("PetFrameDebuff" .. i) local _, icon, count = UnitDebuff("pet", i) if icon then getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon"):SetTexture(icon) local text = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") if count and count > 1 then text:SetText(count) text:Show() else text:Hide() end button:Show() else button:Hide() end end end
-- ref PetFrame_OnUpdate: the attack overlay's alpha ramp — a 0.5 s-per-leg triangle between -- 55/255 and 1, sign-flipped at each end (the ref's own counter shape, transcribed). function PetFrame_OnUpdate(elapsed) local frame = this if not PetAttackModeTexture:IsVisible() then return end local counter = frame.attackModeCounter + elapsed local sign = frame.attackModeSign if counter > 0.5 then sign = -sign frame.attackModeSign = sign end counter = mod(counter, 0.5) frame.attackModeCounter = counter local alpha if sign == 1 then alpha = (55 + (counter * 400)) / 255 else alpha = (255 - (counter * 400)) / 255 end PetAttackModeTexture:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, alpha) end
-- Clicking the pet frame (decision 1066 built the right-hand half). The LEFT button hands -- the pet whatever the cursor is carrying; every other button opens its menu — except for -- the one case that is easy to drop, a RIGHT click with a spell already armed, which puts -- the spell away instead. That exception is the right button's alone: a middle click while -- casting still opens the menu. function PetFrame_OnClick(button) if button ~= "LeftButton" then if button == "RightButton" and SpellIsTargeting() then SpellStopTargeting() else -- No anchor arguments, unlike the player and target frames: this menu opens at -- the CURSOR (ref PetFrame.lua l.128). ToggleDropDownMenu(1, nil, PetFrameDropDown) end return end -- Most specific first: an armed spell binds to the pet, then a held item drops on it -- (this is how you feed one), and with an empty cursor the click simply selects it. if SpellIsTargeting() then SpellTargetUnit("pet") elseif CursorHasItem() then DropItemOnUnit("pet") else TargetUnit("pet") end end
-- The PET menu's owner (ref PetFrame.lua l.158-166). The UnitExists gate is the ref's own, -- and it is not redundant with the frame being hidden: this dropdown is also what the -- TARGET frame's menu falls through to when you have your own pet selected. function PetFrameDropDown_OnLoad() UIDropDownMenu_Initialize(this, PetFrameDropDown_Initialize, "MENU") end
function PetFrameDropDown_Initialize() if UnitExists("pet") then UnitPopup_ShowMenu(PetFrameDropDown, "PET", "pet") end end
function BenillaPetFrame_OnEnter(frame) -- The pet frame is a unit frame in the reference, and takes the same cursor split: -- hovering it with a spell armed lights or greys exactly as the target frame does. if SpellIsTargeting() then if SpellCanTargetUnit("pet") then SetCursor("CAST_CURSOR") else SetCursor("CAST_ERROR_CURSOR") end end if not UnitExists("pet") then return end GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, frame) if GameTooltip:SetUnit("pet") then getglobal("GameTooltipTextLeft1"):SetTextColor(GameTooltip_UnitColor("pet")) end end
